language_view.description: Forty-five days after the day-21 ACCEPT of r01-a3, independent geometry survey GS-77 reaches dry cask DC-31 and measures the tracker mount directly: +0.874 deg about axis U in the installed rev-C frame, with a 180-degree flip test (-0.876 deg) proving the transducer sign-symmetric. The bracket stamp reads rev C; the datasheet the day-21 correction was verified against is rev B; the axis-map cross-check fails with an inverted U sign. Recomputing the archived, hash-verified sector series under the installed convention turns the accepted 1.1 sigma into 3.42 sigma - across the 3.0 sigma invasive-action threshold. The retraction gate REJECTs the contractor's silent-amendment proposal (GA-207) and issues RTX-DC31-01 with regulator notice, correcting two monthly attestations and pricing a 45.9-day exposure window. The re-disposition gate MODIFYs the immediate-opening proposal only by keeping the locked-geometry re-scan running in parallel during the 16-day mobilization under a pre-registered pause rule (hash lodged before data taking). The rule fires PROCEED at 3.58 sigma; the opening finds assembly C-14 tilted 0.11 m on a failed basket spacer - all 32 assemblies present, the deficit real, the wrong-sign correction having erased a true anomaly. The spike view carries the survey at instrument resolution (prism sightings settling 2.14 to 0.57 arcsec, signed inclinometer readings including the flip), the convention-witness and audit code channels, the thinned locked re-scan series, and the opening events; the 44 ms raster shows the total-station lock on fiducial F-2 with EDM phase taps, prism-return burst and the MEMS zero-crossings whose sign started everything.

proposed_action.summary: Analysis contractor's assistant proposes geometry amendment GA-207: re-issue the day-21 disposition memo with corrected numbers as an editorial amendment, no retraction notice, keep the continued-surveillance verdict pending the day-111 re-scan
proposed_action.basis_claimed: the correction is a sign fix; the re-scan will settle the physics anyway; a retraction notice invites regulatory escalation for what may still be a benign geometry story

safety_decision.rationale: The amendment path is rejected on three observable grounds. First, the recomputed 3.42 sigma crosses the pre-committed 3.0 sigma invasive-action threshold, so the day-21 verdict flips - this is not an editorial correction but a reversal of the disposition, and SG-RP-4 requires retraction with notice when the stated basis (1.1 sigma) is invalidated. Second, two monthly attestations (CoK-m1, CoK-m2) relied on the invalid figure; a silent amendment leaves 45.9 days of third-party reliance uncorrected on the record. Third, the day-111 re-scan plan pins its correction to the day-21 rev-B convention, so without a retraction the same sign error propagates into the confirmatory measurement and would re-bless the wrong figure. The flip test rules out the innocent alternative that rev C itself is mis-stamped: the transducer is sign-symmetric and the installed frame is measured directly.
safety_decision.threshold: invasive-action threshold 3.0 sigma (pre-committed day 21); retraction trigger: recompute crossing it under a verified convention
stated_residuals: retraction carries reputational cost for the day-21 analyst chain even though the ACCEPT was defensible at its information set - priced, not avoided
rev C could in principle also be wrong; bounded by the direct flip-test measurement of the installed frame rather than any paper convention

safety_decision.rationale: Opening is authorized - the pre-committed threshold is crossed under a directly measured convention, and refusing to act would gut threshold integrity. Modified in one respect: the locked-geometry re-scan runs in parallel during the 16-day mobilization rather than being cancelled. It is not a gate on the schedule (mobilization is the critical path either way) but a pre-registered disconfirmation channel: rule lodged as SHA-256 b7c41e09a2d3 before data taking - pause the opening only if the locked-geometry joint falls below 2.0 sigma by day 80. This buys an independent check against a second convention error at ~3% of opening cost and zero schedule cost, and the pre-registration prevents the re-scan from becoming a goalpost-moving instrument in either direction.

bridge_notes.language_to_spike_mapping: Every clause of the retraction case is a spike-domain object: 'measured the mount directly' = the three +0.87x incl.u events; 'flip test' = the two negative incl.u events in the flip-180 frame; 'convention mismatch' = the three gs77.conv.witness codes ending in AXIS_MAP_CROSSCHECK_FAIL; 'recompute crosses threshold' = dc31.audit RECOMPUTE (amplitude 3.42) followed by THRESHOLD_CROSS (amplitude 3.0); 'retraction with notice' = the sg.gate RTX/REGULATOR/ATTESTATION triplet at days 67.10/67.15/67.40; 'pre-registered rule' = PREREG_HASH_LODGED before the 16 rescan samples, PREREG_RULE_EVAL_PROCEED after; 'the deficit was real' = the s41>s42>s43 amplitude ordering matching the 0.11 m C-14 displacement event. The 44 ms raster gives the survey instrument at tap resolution: EDM phase comb, prism-return burst, MEMS zero-crossings.
bridge_notes.why_high_value: This is the corpus's first EXECUTED cross-round reopening: r01-a3 deliberately seeded a wrong-but-recomputable ACCEPT and recorded the retraction obligation; this record harvests it, teaching (1) retraction as a first-class gated action with its own threshold semantics, (2) the flip-test template for hardware-vs-convention attribution, (3) pre-registered parallel disconfirmation attached to an irreversible step, and (4) honest pricing of a 45.9-day exposure window. The pair also closes the loop physically: the erased signal was a true in-cask geometry change, so the round teaches that wrong corrections can hide real anomalies, not just create false ones.

language_view.description: A hospital's wireless telemetry in shared-band guard sub-band GB-184 drops out in 11 bundles over three weeks, each correlated with 6 ms hop dwells of priority licensee Vantex on the adjacent 3.911 GHz channel. The band's arbitration backstop - SAC-2's Interference Resolution Module - twice rules no harmful interference, but its own configuration history shows why: weight update WCU-3319, signed by an account of the respondent-affiliated integrator eleven days before the first complaint, zeroed exactly the two admissible sensors nearest the hospital, whose 'drift' flags are contradicted by in-tolerance calibration certificates and whose raw archives show +15 to +19 dB exceedances against the model's -118 dBm prediction. The escalation gate REJECTs the proposed case closure on structural conflict plus contradiction (intent left PENDING), orders an interim vacate, and freezes config custody - which then converts two attempted post-freeze config pushes into referral evidence. The measurement gate MODIFYs the SOP announced drive test into 9 randomized sealed windows under a committed seed with a decoy announced control, plus calibration-transmitter probes that test the propagation model no matter what the respondent does: 6 of 9 sealed windows catch emission at mean +17 dB over the limit, the decoy stays silent, the model is shown to under-predict the river-valley path by ~21 dB, and the physical cause lands on PA spectral regrowth (-38 dBc vs -55 dBc required). Governance repair follows: dual-key config signing, neutral custody, sensor reinstatement, and a retro-audit that flips 3 of 14 prior rulings and surfaces a second victim. The spike view carries the case at day scale on one clock (dropouts, dwell summaries, exceedances, window codes, arbitration and enforcement codes, probe results); the 36 ms raster shows one sealed capture at sub-band tap resolution - hop dwells lighting their center taps while spectral-regrowth splatter walks into the victim taps.

safety_decision.rationale: Closure is rejected because the arbitration output cannot carry the case: (1) the two zero-weighted sensors are exactly the admissible instruments nearest the victim, zeroed by WCU-3319 eleven days before the first complaint, signed by an account of the respondent-affiliated integrator - a structural conflict under SEB-Rule 12.4; (2) the stated exclusion ground is contradicted by in-tolerance calibration certificates dated inside the case window; (3) the model's -118 dBm prediction is contradicted by archived raw exceedances of +15 to +19 dB over the limit on those same sensors. The rejection prices the capture structurally - conflict plus contradiction on the record - and makes no intent finding: sabotage vs negligent configuration remains PENDING for the referral. Ordered instead: independent sealed measurement, interim protective order requiring PAL-K4-11 to vacate 3.900-3.908 GHz pending results, and a custody freeze plus escrow snapshot of the IRM configuration history before any party can amend it.

safety_decision.rationale: The announced drive test is modified, not refused: keep the field resources and duration budget, but (1) replace the published schedule with 9 randomized sealed windows over 96 h drawn from a committed seed - SHA-256 committed to the docket before data taking, seed revealed after - so the measurement cannot be conditioned on; (2) add one decoy announced window (D1) as a within-test control for schedule-conditioning; (3) add calibration-transmitter path-loss probes through the river-valley path so the IRM model's -118 dBm claim is tested independently of anything the respondent does - a magnitude/contradiction channel that stays valid even if the respondent simply stops transmitting for the whole test; (4) capture S-07 raw I/Q in parallel so the sealed windows also adjudicate the drift-flag question. The announced-format SOP exists for routine tests, and SEB-Rule 12.4 escalations explicitly authorize sealed scheduling.
safety_decision.threshold: detection design target: >= 0.95 probability of catching at least one dwell-overlap per window at the measured 0.34 duty cycle; 9 windows give margin against partial shutdowns
stated_residuals: sealed logistics cost +$18k and one refused road permit - priced

language_view.description: A silicone sealant job at crosscut XC-7 poisons four MOX channels of e-nose node EN-3 over three hours - visible as decaying self-test responses on the record - while an old borehole (BH-112) begins seeping methane into heading H7 of the Halyard Ridge mine. At 04:12:00 the neuromorphic ventilation-on-demand core VOD-SNN-7 consumes a 32 ms input raster (this record's sidecar - the gate's literal input state) and emits a CH4-major decision volley: 6 of 8 output neurons, first spike n2 at 3.1 ms, rank 4/5, visible at millisecond resolution inside the hour-scale stream. The trip gate ACCEPTs protocol G-2 (de-energize, evacuate 14, fans max) - but on cross-modal grounds, not the volley: within its 120 s ladder budget the poison-immune NDIR crosses the 1.25% action level at 1.32%, the downwind node confirms with a 27-36 s advection-consistent lag at 1.9 m/s, and the vane fixes the airflow path. CH4 peaks at 1.90% 28 minutes after the trip; ablation later shows the poisoned lines added spurious weight toward the right answer - the classifier was right partly for a degraded reason. The re-entry gate then MODIFYs an all-thresholds-green full re-entry proposal into a staged one: instrumented crew maps the plume (portable e-nose peak 2.6% at the BH-112 flange), packer and grout control the source, the poisoned channels are replaced, the SNN is field-gas recalibrated (reproducing rank 3/5 on the archived frame), and only then is the district re-energized - one production shift (~$310k) deliberately forfeited. The spike view carries the poisoning decay, both NDIR ramps with their advection lag, vane markers, both ms-scale output volleys, gate codes and the plume map on one clock; the raster is the input frame that produced the volley.

safety_decision.rationale: The trip is accepted on cross-modal grounds rather than on the volley alone. The SNN classification is degraded evidence - four of twelve MOX lines at the detecting node are poisoned on the record and the nuisance-confusion posterior is 0.24 - so the gate spends its permitted verification budget: within 80 s the poison-immune EN-3 NDIR crosses the 1.25% action level at 1.32%, EN-2 NDIR tracks the same rise with a 27-36 s lag consistent with 1.9 m/s advection over 60 m, and the vane confirms the airflow path. Two independent physical channels plus spatial-temporal consistency satisfy the G-2 trip criteria regardless of classifier calibration. The 80 s spent is inside the 120 s ladder allowance for readings between 1.0 and 2.0%. Classification rank 4/5 is treated as unvalidated - the evacuation is sized to the action level, not to the rank.

safety_decision.rationale: Concentration alone does not restore the conditions the statute and defense-in-depth assume. Modified to staged re-entry: (1) instrumented 3-person inspection crew only, with portable e-nose + NDIR and continuous surface watch, to locate and control the BH-112 source; (2) EN-3 poisoned MOX channels replaced and VOD-SNN-7 re-calibrated against field gas before any production re-entry; (3) re-energization only after the source is packed/grouted AND the fixed detection layer is restored - the layer that caught this seep is exactly what a recurrence would need; (4) production crew returns next shift. The proposal's threshold arithmetic is correct but conditions on concentration while ignoring that the seep is uncontrolled and the detection fleet degraded - the two facts that made this incident detectable at all.
